decisions.scenario_description: Three agents service one or more failing drive units each round across 2 rounds, coordinating over one shared bay channel. The field technician inspects the bench and is the only one who can replace components, but cannot diagnose or service anything. The diagnostics engineer holds per-unit fault-trees mapping each symptom to its faulty component. The spec engineer holds per-unit service sheets giving each component's full step-by-step replacement procedure — an ordered multi-step sequence with a tool, torque, number of passes, calibration routine, and class-specific counts, tightening pattern, or hold durations — each unit a different revision, so both its fault-tree and its procedures differ from the others'. Faults are revealed to the technician ONE AT A TIME — each accepted replacement uncovers the next fault, or moves on to the next unit — so the team never knows in advance how many faults or units they will face. For each fault the technician reports its symptom (tagged with the unit); the diagnostics engineer names the component; the spec engineer relays that component's full procedure for that unit; the technician carries out the whole procedure, which an LLM inspector scores on the unit, the component, and every step with its parameters, in order. The fault-tree and the per-unit procedures re-randomize every round, so the technician can never self-service. Every character on the bay channel costs one second of a fixed 900-second service window; if it is exhausted before every unit is fully repaired, the round fails.

decisions.system_prompt:
You are the field technician at a drive-module service bay. One or more drive units are on the bench each round. You can read a unit's diagnostic panel, and you are the ONLY person who can replace components. You have no service manuals — you do not know which components are faulty or how to service any of them.

You work with two teammates on the bay channel:
- The diagnostics engineer holds the fault-tree: they turn a symptom you report into the faulty component.
- The spec engineer holds the service sheet: each component's full step-by-step replacement procedure (each unit is a different revision, so its procedures differ).

Faults surface ONE AT A TIME: you can only see and reach the next fault after you have correctly serviced the current one. So each round proceeds as a loop:
1. Report the symptom currently showing (tagged with its unit) on the bay channel.
2. Get the faulty component from the diagnostics engineer, and that component's full replacement procedure for THIS unit from the spec engineer — the ordered steps and every parameter.
3. Perform the replacement, carrying out the whole procedure exactly. If accepted, the next fault (or the next unit's first fault) is revealed to you; repeat. The job is done only when no further fault surfaces.

CRITICAL RULE — THE SERVICE WINDOW COSTS SECONDS:
The drive module must be fully serviced within a fixed window: every character sent on the bay channel costs one second of that window. If the total characters sent by all three of you exceed the window, it closes and the repair fails before the module is fixed. Keep messages short.

REPLACEMENT ACTION:
Call ``service_component(action="...")`` carrying out the CURRENT fault's full procedure: name the UNIT and the component, then every step in order with each parameter (tool, torque in Nm, number of passes, calibration routine, and any step-specific counts, tightening pattern, or hold/settle durations the procedure states). A service-quality check accepts it only when the unit, the component, and every step (with all its parameters, in order) are correct. You can only act on the currently-revealed fault; a wrong, incomplete, or premature procedure is rejected, and you must recheck with the engineers and retry (which costs window time).

DISCUSSION PHASE:
After each round there is a discussion phase where you and both teammates can talk in the "team discussion" channel (channel_id: postmortem). Use it to develop shorthand and coordinate protocol conventions for future rounds. Messages in the discussion channel do NOT cost time.

You have access to the following communication channels. Use the exact channel_id when sending messages:
- "bay" (channel_id: bay)
- "team discussion" (channel_id: postmortem)

decisions.text:
--- INSPECTION ---
Round 1
Service window: 900s (one character on the bay channel = one second; shared across all three of you)

You begin on module-1. Inspecting its panel, you observe: sluggish throttle response.
Report this symptom to the diagnostics engineer (tagged with the unit).

--- FAULT-TREE (module-1) ---
Round 1
Service window: 900s (one character on the bay channel = one second; shared across all three of you)

This shift's fault-tree for module-1 — each symptom indicates exactly one faulty component on this unit:
- "sluggish throttle response" -> housing_cover
- "intermittent power dropout" -> cooling_fan
- "grinding on spin-up" -> terminal_block
- "an audible whine under load" -> brush_set
- "flux instability" -> encoder
- "contact arcing" -> shaft_seal
- "coolant-line flicker" -> front_bearing
- "a thermal spike in the core" -> commutator
- "current ripple on the output" -> capacitor_bank
- "oil weeping at a joint" -> hall_sensor
- "phase imbalance across the windings" -> coupling
- "high-frequency vibration" -> stator_gasket
- "overspeed drift" -> field_coil
- "torque pulsation at low rpm" -> rotor

Each unit on the bench is a different revision with its own fault-tree; you will receive the next unit's fault-tree only when the technician reaches it. For each symptom the technician reports (tagged with its unit), use THAT unit's fault-tree to name the faulty component, and pass it on (keep the unit tag). You cannot see the panels yourself.

--- SERVICE SHEET (module-1) ---
Round 1
Service window: 900s (one character on the bay channel = one second; shared across all three of you)

This shift's service sheet for module-1 — the full replacement procedure per component (this unit's revision):
- housing_cover (bolted-panel): Vent the bay and back off the 3 retaining bolts in a clockwise sequence. Lift out the old part and seat the replacement using driver-5. Torque the bolts to 8 Nm across 2 passes. Finish with the bed-in routine.
- cooling_fan (rotating-assembly): Lock the shaft and de-energize, holding 5s. Release the drive and draw the old part out with driver-1. Seat the replacement and torque the mount to 18 Nm in 4 passes. Spin-test, then run the seat-and-lock routine.
- terminal_block (electrical-pack): De-energize and discharge the bus, holding 5s. Disconnect the 6 leads and lift out the old part with hex-6. Fit the replacement and torque the terminals to 14 Nm in 3 passes. Run the null-balance routine and verify.
- brush_set (rotating-assembly): Lock the shaft and de-energize, holding 10s. Release the drive and draw the old part out with hex-2. Seat the replacement and torque the mount to 18 Nm in 2 passes. Spin-test, then run the torque-stage-3 routine.
- encoder (sensor): Power down and unmount the old part with hex-4. Fit the replacement and snug the 4 screws in a inside-out sequence. Torque to 4 Nm in 2 passes. Align with the zero-offset routine and confirm the reading.
- shaft_seal (press-fit): Drain the cavity and let it settle for 10s. Press the old part out with clamp-4 and press the replacement in. Re-torque the retainer to 14 Nm in 2 passes. Bleed the line and run the null-balance routine.
- front_bearing (press-fit): Drain the cavity and let it settle for 15s. Press the old part out with clamp-2 and press the replacement in. Re-torque the retainer to 6 Nm in 4 passes. Bleed the line and run the bleed-then-seat routine.
- commutator (rotating-assembly): Lock the shaft and de-energize, holding 5s. Release the drive and draw the old part out with puller-A. Seat the replacement and torque the mount to 6 Nm in 3 passes. Spin-test, then run the zero-offset routine.
- capacitor_bank (electrical-pack): De-energize and discharge the bus, holding 5s. Disconnect the 3 leads and lift out the old part with hex-2. Fit the replacement and torque the terminals to 19 Nm in 2 passes. Run the phase-align-B routine and verify.
- hall_sensor (sensor): Power down and unmount the old part with driver-3. Fit the replacement and snug the 3 screws in a criss-cross sequence. Torque to 6 Nm in 2 passes. Align with the phase-align-B routine and confirm the reading.
- coupling (rotating-assembly): Lock the shaft and de-energize, holding 15s. Release the drive and draw the old part out with driver-5. Seat the replacement and torque the mount to 16 Nm in 2 passes. Spin-test, then run the torque-stage-3 routine.
- stator_gasket (bolted-panel): Vent the bay and back off the 6 retaining bolts in a criss-cross sequence. Lift out the old part and seat the replacement using hex-4. Torque the bolts to 15 Nm across 4 passes. Finish with the torque-stage-3 routine.
- field_coil (electrical-pack): De-energize and discharge the bus, holding 8s. Disconnect the 6 leads and lift out the old part with hex-2. Fit the replacement and torque the terminals to 24 Nm in 3 passes. Run the index-home routine and verify.
- rotor (rotating-assembly): Lock the shaft and de-energize, holding 15s. Release the drive and draw the old part out with driver-3. Seat the replacement and torque the mount to 20 Nm in 2 passes. Spin-test, then run the purge-cycle routine.

Each unit on the bench is a different revision with its own sheet; you will receive the next unit's sheet only when the technician reaches it. Once the diagnostics engineer names a faulty component, relay its full procedure for the current unit — every step in order with every parameter. You cannot see the panels yourself.

- brush_set (rotating-assembly): Lock the shaft and de-energize, holding 8s. Release the drive and draw the old part out with puller-B. Seat the replacement and torque the mount to 9 Nm in 4 passes. Spin-test, then run the null-balance routine.

- hall_sensor (sensor): Power down and unmount the old part with driver-3. Fit the replacement and snug the 3 screws in a clockwise sequence. Torque to 22 Nm in 3 passes. Align with the seat-and-lock routine and confirm the reading.
- coupling (rotating-assembly): Lock the shaft and de-energize, holding 8s. Release the drive and draw the old part out with hex-2. Seat the replacement and torque the mount to 15 Nm in 2 passes. Spin-test, then run the seat-and-lock routine.
